resale_co.name: Certificate of Resale (Certificate of Continued Occupancy / CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Little Ferry Building Department (Construction Official)
requirements: Inspection of the unit by the Building Department; nobody may occupy the home before Building Department approval
All open building permits must be closed, and all taxes, penalties and fees due to the Borough must be paid; the Tax Office signs off that taxes are current
Buyer signs a notarized Certificate in Lieu of Oath stating the number of dwelling units (no illegal units; basement may not be used as a dwelling or sleeping area; short-term rentals prohibited)
Owner (not the realtor) signs the Smoke/CO Detectors, Fire Door and Fire Extinguisher Affidavit
Smoke detectors as required for the year built, on every level and near sleeping areas; detectors over 10 years old replaced; battery-only units must be 10-year sealed

Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of sleeping areas, on every level, outside any room with a fuel-burning appliance and near an attached garage entrance; CO detectors over 5 years old replaced unless the manufacturer allows longer
ABC fire extinguisher rated at least 2A:10B:C within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor (form still lists it)
Buyer fills out the Police Department emergency contact form
Construction Official certifies whether there are open permits

fees.label: Certificate of Resale, per unit
fees.quote: Submit a check payable to the Borough of Little Ferry for $100/unit for Resale, Inspections that fail are subject to additional fees.

fees.label: Resale certificate, per dwelling unit (Borough Code 13-1.6)
fees.quote: Fee for certificate of compliance for rentals or resale certificate$100 per dwelling unit

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Application for a Certificate of Resale from the Building Department page, fill out every page (owner affidavit, buyer's notarized Certificate in Lieu of Oath, Tax Office sign-off, Police emergency contact form) and submit it with a check for $100 per unit payable to the Borough of Little Ferry at Borough Hall, 215-217 Liberty Street (Monday to Friday 8:30am to 4:30pm). Give the name and phone of the person who will meet the inspector. Permit and inspection requests also run through the SDL Portal linked on the Building Department page.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Code Official (technical assistant: Bertha Sneyer, 201-641-2942, b-sneyer@littleferrynj.org)

No one is permitted to occupy the premises prior to approval from the Building Department.
A CCO will only be issued once all open building permits are closed; and all taxes, penalties and/or fees due to the Borough are paid.

resale_co.notes: The Borough's Certificate of Resale application (scanned PDF dated 8-21-25 in its file name, citing Ordinances 1605-19-23 and 1272-04-09) is the main source; it is an image scan, so a text check cannot read it. The ordinance text that creates the resale certificate was not found in the online code (the ecode360 code shows only the $100 fee in Section 13-1.6 and rental CCO rules in Chapter 35). No timing, lead time or validity period is published. A separate Certificate of Rental application exists for rentals; rental CCO rules are not resale requirements.

requirements: Smoke detectors placed according to the year the house was built (battery 10-year sealed units allowed for pre-1977 homes; 110V interconnected units for newer homes), on each level and within 10 feet of sleeping rooms
Smoke detectors with a manufacture date over 10 years must be replaced
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of sleeping areas, on every level, outside rooms with fuel-burning appliances and near an attached garage entrance
ABC fire extinguisher rated at least 2A:10B:C within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)
Owner or building management (not the realtor) signs the Smoke/CO Detectors, Fire Door and Fire Extinguisher Affidavit

authorities.name: Borough of Little Ferry Building Department (smoke/CO checked as part of the Certificate of Resale)
authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke, CO and extinguisher requirements and the owner affidavit are pages of the Certificate of Resale application filed with the Building Department.

evidence.quote: Smoke/Carbon Dioxide (CO) Detectors / Fire Door / Fire Extinguisher Requirements
Note: This form must be completed by the OWNER or BUILDING MANAGEMENT. Realtors are prohibited from filling out this form.

authorities.name: NJ Division of Fire Safety (listed in the NJ DCA directory as the smoke detector compliance office for Little Ferry)
authorities.how_to_apply: Call the number listed in the state directory, (609) 633-6132, to confirm whether a state-issued certificate is needed in addition to the Borough's resale inspection.

evidence.quote: LEAID: 0230-001 Little Ferry Boro SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: NJ Division Fire Safety Enf Auth. Municipal Addr: PO Box 809 Trenton NJ 08625-0809 Fire Official William R Holley Phone (609) 633-6132

fire_cert.notes: Little Ferry's code (Section 20-1) makes the Fire Department's Bureau of Fire Prevention the local fire code agency, but it does not cover owner-occupied 1-2 family homes, and no Borough page offers a separate smoke/CO certificate application. The Borough's resale application includes the smoke/CO/extinguisher checklist and owner affidavit. The NJ DCA fire directory (survey 2/27/2026) lists the local fire official as William R Holley, (201) 641-9234, wrhdpw1@gmail.com, but names the NJ Division of Fire Safety as the smoke detector compliance office, which conflicts with the Borough form. The Borough form still lists a fire extinguisher; the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19).

other_items.label: Taxes and Borough fees current
other_items.detail: The Tax Office must sign that taxes are current, and all taxes, penalties and fees due to the Borough must be paid before the CCO is issued.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: The Construction Official certifies whether there are open permits; all must be closed before the CCO is issued.

other_items.label: Buyer's Certificate in Lieu of Oath (unit count)
other_items.detail: The buyer signs a notarized statement of how many dwelling units the house has, agreeing not to rent part of a single-family home or convert it without telling the Construction Department.

other_items.label: Police emergency contact form
other_items.detail: The buyer fills out the Police Department emergency contact form included in the resale packet.

open_questions: Does the NJ Division of Fire Safety issue a separate smoke/CO certificate for Little Ferry sales, or does the Borough's resale inspection cover it?
How far ahead of closing should the resale application be filed, and how long is the certificate valid?
What is the reinspection fee after a failed inspection?
Does Little Ferry still require the fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19?
